land.text: the Khazar country north of the Caucasus, a client of the Western Turks until the murder of Tong Yabghu c. 630

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by Western Turkic Khaganate; Old Great Bulgaria'. Old Great Bulgaria did not precede the Khazars on the same land: the Khazars took its steppe in 668.

land.text: Sarkel on the lower Don, Belaya Vyezha

successors.note: Sviatoslav, c. 965; the Rus' did not occupy the heartland.

land.text: the steppes of southeast Europe that the Pechenegs 'controlled' in the 9th and 10th centuries

successors.note: No Cliopatria row and no dossier yet; Pechenegs page gives no date for their taking the former Khazar steppe.
Khazars page infobox 'Succeeded by Cumania, Pechenegs, Kievan Rus', Durdzuks, Volga Bulgaria, Alania'; no dossier yet.

capitals.name: Balanjar (site disputed, Dagestan)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Balanjar (c. 650-c. 720)'; Balanjar page: a capital of the Baranjar state in the 630s, in the Khazar Khaganate from c. 650, 'until the early 720s'. Site 'probably on the lower Sulak River' (Artamonov: Buynaksk, later ruins south of Makhachkala); the point is Buynaksk from the gazetteer, a placeholder within about 50 km.

capitals.name: Samandar (Dagestan, Kizlyar or Tarki)
capitals.note: 'became the second capital of the Khazar Khaganate in the 720s', infobox 720-750; Samandar page: moved to Atil 'between 730 and 750'. Site 'generally assumed' in Dagestan, Kizlyar or Tarki proposed; the point is Makhachkala (Tarki), a placeholder. Return pass: Samandar page (re-read): no coordinates; 'The exact location of Samandar has not been identified', 'midway between Derbent and Atil, near the shore of the Caspian Sea'; Kizlyar and Tarki proposed, 'Tarki corresponds more closely to medieval sources'. The point is Tarki; it lies 15-30 km outside Cliopatria's 723 shape because that shape stops short of the coast (a shape fault, not a site fault), and it is kept.

capitals.name: Atil (Itil, Volga delta)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Atil (750-c. 965-969)'; 'in the Volga Delta region'. The 2008 Samosdelka identification 'has since been disproven'; the gazetteer's Itil point is a placeholder in the delta.

keyframe_review.note: 630-632, 0.32 M km2 (1,241 cells: Dagestan, the Terek and the Kalmyk steppe). Khazars page: an embryonic state formed 'sometime after 630' out of the Göktürk breakup, infobox 'Established c. 650'; Tong Yabghu page: after his murder client tribes such as the Khazars and Great Bulgaria became independent. Balanjar page: in the 630s Balanjar was 'a capital of the Baranjar state' and in c. 650 the city became part of the Khazar Khaganate with the rest of the Baranjar domains, so the 630 core may be the Baranjar state's land. The shape stands (page silent on borders); the infobox gives no area for this age.
633-637, 0.32 M km2, the 630 core within 5 cells; no page moves it.
638-646, 0.32 M km2, the 630 core within 2 cells. Arab-Khazar wars page: Derbent passed to the Arabs in 642 (Shahrbaraz's surrender), which is just outside this shape's 48.2 E edge.

647-655, 0.47 M km2: the core plus 532 cells of the lower Volga and the Ural-Aral steppe (Astrakhan, Volgograd, west Kazakhstan; 114 of them inside the Western Turk 646 shape). Khazars page: the khaganate dominated, c. 650-965, 'from the Volga-Don steppes to the eastern Crimea' and the northern Caucasus; it gives no year for the growth. Year and extent are Cliopatria's and stand unverified (ledger gain, confidence 1). Return pass: the ledger now splits the gain: 114 cells from western-gokturks (the cells inside the Western Turk 646 shape) and 418 from nobody.

656-673, 0.47 M km2, the 647 shape. Old Great Bulgaria page: the state 'disintegrated under Khazar attack in 668'; Khazars page: the Onoghur-Bulghar union subjugated 'sometime around 670'. The shape holds to 667; the western steppe is added from 668 (next keyframe).

correction.text: the shape as drawn, for 656-667 only; from 668 the khazaria_668 keyframe holds

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 668-673, 0.72 M km2: the 674 shape six years early. Old Great Bulgaria page and Asparukh's page: 'the state disintegrated under Khazar attack in 668'; the Khazars page puts the subjugation of the Onoghur-Bulghar union 'sometime around 670' and has the Khazars 'dominated the Crimea (650-c. 950)'. 981 of the 1,018 cells added in 674 lie in Old Great Bulgaria's 656-673 shape, so the gain is Old Great Bulgaria's steppe between the Don and the Dnieper, the Kuban and the Crimea; the Danube-Dniester remnant (Asparukh's horde, Old Great Bulgaria 674 shape) stays outside.

correction.text: the 674 shape: the Pontic steppe from the Don to the Dnieper, the Kuban, the north Caucasus and the Crimea added to the Khazar core

keyframe_review.note: 674-681, 0.72 M km2. The shape is right from 668 (previous keyframe); Cliopatria's 674 is six years late. Khazars page: 'between the Danube and the Dniepr' is the western limit named for c. 670; the shape's west edge (31.8 E) is the Dnieper.

682-723, 0.75 M km2: the 674 shape plus 136 cells (88% Pontic steppe, 51% Volga region). No page dates or explains the growth; shape stands as unverified, ledger gain at confidence 1. Infobox 1.0 M km2 for 900 and 3.0 M km2 for 850 are later than this shape.

724-731, 0.76 M km2: the 682 shape plus 32 cells in Shirvan and Caucasian Albania south of Derbent (28 in Azerbaijan). Arab-Khazar wars page: Derbent recovered by the Arabs in 713/714 and again entered by al-Jarrah in 722; Balanjar stormed on 21 August 722; in February 724 al-Jarrah beat the Khazars between the Kura and Araxes; the Khazars won at Ardabil on 7-9 December 730 and raided as far as Mosul; Maslama retook Albania in early 731. The strip is the war zone (contest in the ledger, 722-737), not Khazar land; the page calls the raids plunder, not conquest.

correction.text: the 682 shape without the Caucasian strip south of Derbent, which is the contested zone of the Second Arab-Khazar War

keyframe_review.note: 732-740, 0.75 M km2, the 682 shape within 30 cells: after 731 the Arabs hold Derbent (24,000 troops garrisoned) 'leaving the North Caucasus in Khazar hands' (page).
741-749, 0.75 M km2, one cell different from 732.

750-762, 0.75 M km2. Atil becomes the capital (infobox 750; Atil page 'from the mid-8th century'); Umayyad fall in 750 and 'largely peaceful' relations with the Caucasus Muslims afterwards (Arab-Khazar wars page). Infobox area 3.0 M km2 is for 850.

763-767, 0.80 M km2, the largest Cliopatria shape: the 750 shape plus 212 cells in Georgia, Azerbaijan, Armenia and Iberia (Transcaucasia 28% of its cells). Khazars page: Ras Tarkhan raided Transcaucasia in 762-764 after the failed Abbasid marriage; Arab-Khazar wars page: 'two Khazar raids in the 760s and 799' interrupted the peace. A raid holds no ground, so the strip comes out; the raid is a war with empty zones.

correction.text: the 750 shape without the Transcaucasian strip raided in 762-764

keyframe_review.note: 768-777, 0.75 M km2, the 750 shape again.
778-813, 0.75 M km2, +1 cell; no event moves the border.

840-865, 0.75 M km2, +8/-5 cells. Infobox area 3.0 M km2 for 850 against 0.75 M km2 here (ratio 0.25, beyond a factor of two): the page counts the peoples who paid tribute 'between the Caucasus, the Aral Sea, the Ural Mountains, and the Ukrainian steppes'; the shape is the core and the tributaries have no dated borders on the pages (the Volga Bulgars as 'protectorate' are a vassal event; the Magyars, Slavs and Burtas are not dated). Around 830 'a rebellion broke out in the Khazar khaganate' (Kabars to the Magyars; Hungarians page). Return pass: Levedia page (re-read) names none of the tributary Slav peoples and dates no Khazar rule over the Magyars ('Modern historians propose periods of 20 to 300 years'; Porphyrogenitus: they 'lived together with the Chazars for three years'; settlement before 750 or around 830); the Khazars page dates only the rebellion 'around 830' and the Alan incitement 'around 900'. No tributary can be dated to a year, so no vassal event is written and the 0.75 M km2 stands against the infobox's 3.0 M km2.
866-874, 0.75 M km2, +1 cell. Pechenegs on the Donets and Kuban from the 830s-850s (Pechenegs page), some Kuban groups 'forced to acknowledge the Khazars supremacy'; no loss is dated.

888-895, 0.75 M km2. Pechenegs page: by 889 they were 'Driven further west by the Khazars and Cumans' and by 892 they 'drove the Magyars west of the Dnieper River'; the page gives no Khazar loss, so the Pontic steppe stays in the shape (a gap: Pechenegs 'controlled much of the steppes of southeast Europe and the Crimean Peninsula' in the 9th and 10th centuries). Return pass: Etelköz page (re-read): the Magyars' stay there is about 850-895, a new Pecheneg invasion made them leave 'around 895' (Simeon I persuaded the Pechenegs); the page does not say the Pechenegs took the Pontic steppe and does not mention a Khazar loss; the Khazars page says Khazar control of the Middle Dnieper from Kiev declined 'by the 880s'. No dated loss, so the steppe stays Khazar to 965 (gap).
896-910, 0.75 M km2. Infobox 1.0 M km2 for 900: ratio 0.75, within a factor of two.
911-946, 0.75 M km2, +2 cells; 913 Varangian raid on the Caspian and the closing of the Volga passage (page) moves no border.

960-969, 0.75 M km2. Sviatoslav's campaign (c. 964-969, its chronology 'uncertain and disputed') destroyed Sarkel 'around 965' and set up the Rus' settlement of Belaya Vyezha; Atil fell 'c. 968 or 969'. The shape holds for 960-964; Sarkel on the Don comes out from 965 (next keyframe).

correction.text: the shape as drawn, for 960-964 only

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 965-969, 0.74 M km2: the 960 shape without Sarkel and the lower Don. The Khazars page: 'Sarkel fell in 965'; Sviatoslav page: destroyed 'around 965', with Atil destroyed afterward (Artamonov and Christian reverse the order); Atil sacked 'c. 968 or 969' (Atil page: '968 or 969 CE').

correction.text: the 960 shape without Sarkel and the Don below Voronezh: 'Sarkel fell in 965'

keyframe_review.note: 970-979, 0.32 M km2 (the 630 core again: Dagestan, Terek, Kalmyk steppe). The Khazars page puts the end at Atil's sack 'c. 968 or 969' (infobox 969); the Sviatoslav page says Khazar successor statelets 'continued their precarious existence in the region' without a border, and the Khazars page has Khazars named in 986, 1016 and 1083. No page gives a Khazar border after 969, so no state is drawn from 970: the dossier ends in 969 and the successors take the land. The shape is a rump with no dated frontier (gap for a successor-statelet dossier).

correction.text: years only: the shape belongs to no year of this dossier (the state ended in 969); its land passes to the successors (Alania in the north Caucasus, the Pechenegs and Oghuz on the steppe, the Rus' at Sarkel) and the Khazar remnants have no dossier

region.text: the Khazar country north of the Caucasus: the Terek, the Kuma and the Kalmyk steppe

ledger.note: 630: the Khazars stand on the Caspian gate. An embryonic state formed 'sometime after 630' out of the Göktürk breakup (infobox: 'Established c. 650'); Tong Yabghu page: client tribes such as the Khazars and Great Bulgaria became independent on his murder (c. 630). Cliopatria's 630 core is Dagestan, the Terek and the Kalmyk steppe.

region.text: Dagestan, the Caspian gate around Balanjar

ledger.note: 630: the Derbent country (Dagestan) passes from the Western Turks. The Tong Yabghu page names no Khazar holding of Dagestan; the year and the land are Cliopatria's 630 shape, which includes Dagestan. Balanjar, in Dagestan, is the Khazar capital in the Khazars page's infobox from c. 650. Derbent page (re-read): it gives no year for a Khazar hold of Derbent or Dagestan; the Turkic sack of Derbent is 627 and the Arab capture 643.

region.text: Derbent and the Caspian gate up to Balanjar

ledger.note: 642: the Arabs reach the Caspian gate. 'The first attack on Derbent was launched in 642 under Suraqa ibn Amr'; the Persian governor Shahrbaraz's surrender was ratified by Caliph Umar, so Derbent passed to the Arabs; early raids reached 'as far as al-Bayda on the Volga', a claim the page says modern scholars dispute. The Derbent page (re-read) gives 643 for the Arab capture of Derbent; the Arab-Khazar wars page, the specialised article, gives the first attack in 642 and is kept.

region.text: the Ural steppe north-east of the Caspian (west Kazakhstan, 52.6-54.5 E, 45.4-48.2 N), Cliopatria's Western Göktürks land of 646

ledger.note: 647: 114 cells (about 28,800 km2, 96 of them in the Kazakh Steppe) pass from the Western Göktürks to Khazaria in Cliopatria's shapes. The Khazars page has the khaganate dominating c. 650-965 'from the Volga-Don steppes' but dates no step and names no Western Turk loss, so the year and the land are Cliopatria's. Mirror of western-gokturks' 647 loss to khazaria (review fix).

region.text: the lower Volga, the Ural-Aral steppe and the Volga-Don steppe east of the core, without the Western Turk land of 646

ledger.note: 647: the lower Volga and the Ural-Aral steppe join the Khazar country. The page has the khaganate dominating, c. 650-965, the land 'from the Volga-Don steppes to the eastern Crimea' and the north Caucasus but dates no step; the year and the 418 cells (532 minus the 114 from the Western Göktürks) are Cliopatria's. Re-read on the return pass: still no date and no route on the Khazars page.

region.text: Derbent and the Caspian gate up to Balanjar

ledger.note: 652: the Khazars hold the Caspian gate. 'the Arabs were defeated at Balanjar, 'a decisive defeat for the Arabs': 'Abd al-Rahman and 4,000 of his troops were killed'; the Arabs keep Derbent and large-scale hostilities pause until the early 8th century.

region.text: the Pontic steppe between the Don and the Dnieper, the Kuban and the Crimea, Old Great Bulgaria's country

ledger.note: 668: the Khazars break Old Great Bulgaria. 'The state disintegrated under Khazar attack in 668' (Old Great Bulgaria page, Asparukh page); Khazars page: the Onoghur-Bulghar union subjugated 'sometime around 670'. The region is the researcher's reading: 981 of the 1,018 cells Cliopatria adds in 674 lie in Old Great Bulgaria's shape.

region.text: a strip of the Pontic steppe and the Volga region

ledger.note: 682: a further 136 cells of the Pontic and Volga steppe. The pages say nothing of 682; the year and cells are Cliopatria's 682 shape (First Bulgarian Empire begins the same year to the west). Re-read on the return pass: the Khazars page has the Khaghanate 'properly constituted' around 670, the Bulgar migration to the Danube c. 679 and a raid of 683-685, and says nothing of a 682 growth; the 136 cells stay Cliopatria's (confidence 1).

region.text: Derbent and the Albanian strip south of it, the front of 722-737

ledger.note: 722: the Second Arab-Khazar War reaches the Caspian gate. Thirty thousand Khazars invade Armenia in the winter of 721/722 and beat the Arabs at Marj al-Hijara; al-Jarrah then enters Derbent without resistance and the Arabs take Balanjar, 'storming the city on 21 August 722'. The Khazars win at Ardabil on 7-9 December 730 and the Arabs retake Albania in 731 (zone: Derbent and the Albanian strip Cliopatria draws in 724-731).

722: the capital leaves Balanjar. Balanjar page: after the attack of c. 722 or 723 the 'capital of Khazaria was thereafter moved to Samandar and later to Atil'; Samandar page: Samandar 'became the second capital of the Khazar Khaganate in the 720s'; the infobox has Samandar 720-750.

region.text: Derbent and the Albanian strip south of it

ledger.note: 737: Marwan's invasion ends the war. Marwan's two-pronged advance met the Khazars at Samandar and reached al-Bayda ('The khagan withdrew towards the Ural Mountains'); afterwards Derbent stays 'the northernmost outpost of the Muslim world' and the North Caucasus 'in Khazar hands' (page infobox). The excerpt does not give the terms; the Khazars page has the khagan forced to accept conversion to Islam, undone within three years.
750: the capital moves to Atil on the Volga delta. Infobox 'Atil (750-c. 965-969)'; Atil page 'from the mid-8th century'; Samandar page puts the move 'sometime between 730 and 750'.

c. 890: the Volga Bulgars as Khazar vassals. The Volga Bulgaria infobox: 'Vassals of the Khazars (late 9th century-969)'; the article says the Bulgars 'came under the overlordship of Khazars' without a year; the Khazars page calls the Volga Bulgarians a 'protectorate'. 890 is the researcher's mid-point of 'late 9th century'. Almış page (re-read): Almış ruled the Volga Bulgars 'c. 895-925' and was 'initially a vassal of the Khazars'; the page gives no year for the start of the suzerainty, so 890 stays a mid-point (confidence 1).

region.text: Sarkel on the lower Don, which the Rus' made Belaya Vyezha

ledger.note: 965: Sviatoslav destroys Sarkel. he destroyed it 'around 965' and set up a Rus' settlement called Belaya Vyezha (Sviatoslav page, chronology 'uncertain and disputed'); Khazars page: 'Sarkel fell in 965'. Fortress on the lower Don at about 47.7 N, 42.2 E.

969: the Volga Bulgars cease to be Khazar vassals. Infobox 'Vassals of the Khazars (late 9th century-969)'; 'complete independence was reached after Khazaria's destruction and conquest by Sviatoslav in the late 10th century'.

969: Sviatoslav sacks Atil and the Khazar khaganate ends. Infobox 'sacking and razing of Atil: 969'; text 'c. 968 or 969'; Atil page '968 or 969 CE'. Khazar statelets lingered ('precarious existence', Sviatoslav page; Khazars named in 1016 and 1083) without a border any page gives. The Pontic steppe passes to the Pechenegs and the Oghuz, the Don to the Rus', the Volga to the independent Bulgars, the north Caucasus to Alania.

wars.name: First Arab-Khazar War

zones.text: Derbent and the Caspian gate up to Balanjar

wars.outcome: The Arabs take Derbent in 642; the Khazars crush an Arab army at Balanjar in 652 and the Arabs fall back to Derbent; hostilities pause until the early 8th century.
wars.note: 'Abd al-Rahman and 4,000 of his troops were killed'; the Arab claim that his cavalry reached al-Bayda on the Volga is disputed by modern scholars.

wars.name: Khazar conquest of Old Great Bulgaria

zones.text: the Pontic steppe between the Don and the Dnieper, the Kuban and the Crimea

wars.outcome: Old Great Bulgaria disintegrates under Khazar attack (668); the Bulgars scatter: Batbayan subject to the Khazars, Kotrag north on the Volga, Asparukh west to the Danube delta.
wars.note: Khazars page: the union subjugated 'sometime around 670'.

wars.name: Second Arab-Khazar War
wars.outcome: The Arabs hold Derbent, Albania and Iberia (Tiflis 724) and end at Derbent 'the northernmost outpost of the Muslim world', leaving the North Caucasus to the Khazars; Marwan's 737 invasion drives the khagan towards the Urals; Byzantine-Khazar alliance sealed by the 733 marriage of Constantine V to Tzitzak.
wars.note: Khazars win at Ardabil on 7-9 December 730 (al-Jarrah killed) and raid to Mosul; Maslama's Derbent colony of 24,000 troops in 731; the page's excerpt ends before the terms of 737.

wars.name: Khazar raids on Transcaucasia
wars.outcome: A raid by Ras Tarkhan after the failed Abbasid marriage alliance; no ground held.
wars.note: The Arab-Khazar wars page counts 'two Khazar raids in the 760s and 799'. Cliopatria's 763-767 shape draws the raided strip as Khazar land; the dossier does not.

wars.name: Khazar raids of 799
wars.outcome: A series of Khazar raids breaks the relations between the Khazars and the Abbasids; no ground held or lost.
wars.note: Khazars page: 'relations between the Khazars and the Abbasids were ultimately broken by a series of raids which occurred in 799'. The Arab-Khazar wars page (re-read) says only 'two Khazar raids in the 760s and 799'; neither page names a leader, the region raided or an Abbasid reply.

wars.name: Pecheneg and Oghuz wars
wars.outcome: The Oghuz defeat the Pechenegs near the Aral Sea before 850; the Khazars ally with the Oghuz against them; the Pechenegs settle on the Donets and Kuban and by 889-892 drive the Magyars west of the Dnieper. No Khazar loss is dated.
wars.note: Pecheneg westward migration c. 830 (Pritsak) or not before the 850s (Kristo). Hungarians page: c. 830 Kabar tribes of the Khazars join the Magyars in Etelkoz; the first Pecheneg attack c. 854; King Benjamin fought 'the allied forces of five lands' c. 880-890 (Khazars page).

wars.name: Sviatoslav's campaign against the Khazars
wars.outcome: Rus' victory: Vyatichi made tributary to Kiev (966), Sarkel destroyed around 965, Atil sacked 968 or 969; no permanent Rus' occupation of the heartland.
wars.note: The Sviatoslav page calls the chronology 'uncertain and disputed' and gives no date for Samandar's sack (Samandar page: 'in the 960s').

certainty.note: Steppe and mountain frontiers throughout; the only fixed line is the Arab-held fortress of Derbent from 737 ('the northernmost outpost of the Muslim world'), a fortress and not a surveyed border. The tribute lands between the Caucasus, the Aral Sea and the Urals have no borders on any page.

notes:
Cliopatria row Khazaria 630..979 (25 shapes). The state ends in 969 (Atil sacked 'c. 968 or 969', infobox 969) instead of 979: the 970-979 shape (the 630 core) is marked wrong because no page draws a Khazar frontier after 969. Pages describe Khazar statelets lingering ('precarious existence', Sviatoslav page) and the Khazars page has Khazars named in 986, 1016, 1083 and 'fade from history' in 1106; a gap-filler may add a rump.

Shape changes explained: 647 (+532 cells, lower Volga and Ural-Aral steppe) and 682 (+136 cells) rest on Cliopatria alone (confidence 1); 674 (+1,018 cells, Pontic steppe and Crimea) is the Khazar conquest of Old Great Bulgaria, dated 668 by the Bulgaria pages (the Khazars page says c. 670) and moved six years earlier in a new keyframe; 724-731 and 763-767 are war and raid zones south of the Caucasus, taken out of the shape; 970 is the end. All the other transitions are changes of 1-9 cells.

Area check: the infobox gives 3.0 M km2 for 850 and 1.0 M km2 for 900; shapes are 0.75 M km2 throughout, so the 850 figure is 4 times larger than the shape (it counts the tribute-paying peoples), the 900 figure within a factor of two. The tributaries have no dated borders on the pages opened: the Volga Bulgars are a vassal event; the Magyars (subordinates of the Khazars in the early 8th century, Hungarians page, until the c. 830 Kabar rebellion), the Burtas and the Slavic tribes (Vyatichi tribute to Kiev instead of the Khazars in 966, Sviatoslav page) have no dated start and are not drawn.

Gaps: Pecheneg pressure (Donets and Kuban from the 830s-850s, west of the Dnieper by 892) is not dated as a Khazar loss, so the Pontic steppe stays Khazar to 965 in the corrected keyframes; Alan and Georgian-border events; Justinian II's escape (704-705) and the 733 Byzantine marriage move no border; Crimea 'dominated (650-c. 950)' and Cherson 'wrested back in the 10th century' are undated steps. Capital coordinates for Balanjar, Samandar and Atil are placeholders (sites not fixed). Wikipedia's Khazars page calls the state 'Khazar Khaganate' and the 'Khazar Correspondence' authentic; no ruler list with reign years exists on it, so no ruler strip.

Counterparts needing dossiers: pechenegs (c. 830s-1091, steppe, no Cliopatria row), alania (north Caucasus, 9th century-1239). Old Great Bulgaria and Volga Bulgaria exist in Cliopatria; first-bulgarian-empire starts 682.

Return pass (review ia-01-d, 2026-10-18). (1) The 647 gain is split: 114 cells from western-gokturks (the cells of Cliopatria's Western Göktürks 646 shape that its Khazaria 647 shape holds, 96 of them in the Kazakh Steppe) and 418 from nobody; the western-gokturks dossier carries the mirror 647 loss and no longer draws the 114 cells for 647-657.
